title: Accounting Applications Series (ACT) - Performance Indicators
note: Tier 1 and Tier 2 indicators are in overall_finance_exam.json. This file contains Tier 3 Accounting Pathway indicators.

Business Law (BL).standard: Understands business's responsibility to know, abide by, and enforce laws and regulations that affect business operations and transactions

indicators.text: Explain financial disclosure regulations and policies
Comply with financial reporting and internal control regulations in accounting
Discuss state regulation of the accounting industry
Comply with state regulations

Financial Analysis (FI).standard: Understands tools, strategies, and systems used to maintain, monitor, control, and plan the use of financial resources

indicators.text: Discuss the nature of the accounting cycle
Distinguish among types of business transactions
Distinguish among types of business documentation
Demonstrate the effects of transactions on the accounting equation
Prepare a chart of accounts
Explain the nature of special journals
Journalize business transactions
Post journal entries to general ledger accounts
Prepare a trial balance
Journalize and post adjusting entries
Journalize and post closing entries
Prepare a post-closing trial balance
Identify and correct accounting errors
Prepare worksheets
Explain cash control procedures (signature cards, deposit slips, internal/external controls, cash clearing, etc.)
Reconcile cash
Account for petty cash
Account for cash receipts (record cash, record income)
Account for cash payments (record cash, record expenses)
Explain the nature of accounts payable
Account for purchases (purchase requisitions, purchase orders, invoices, vouchers, etc.)
Process accounts payable (maintain vendor file, post to ledger, process invoices and checks)
Explain the nature of accounts receivable
Account for sales (invoices, sales receipts, etc.)
Process accounts receivable (post to ledger, process payment, process uncollectible account, etc.)
Record inventory transactions
Process inventory adjustments (shrinkage, obsolescence, returns, etc.)
Explain methods used to value inventory (FIFO, LIFO, average cost, etc.)
Determine the cost/value of inventory
Explain the nature of payroll expenses (Social Security tax, Medicare tax, FUTA, SUTA, workers' compensation, etc.)
Maintain employee earnings records (timecards, time sheets, etc.)
Calculate employee earnings
Calculate employee deductions
Calculate payroll taxes
Account for payroll transactions (earnings, taxes, benefits, other deductions)
Process payroll payments and remittances (employees, benefits, taxes)
Prepare federal, state, and local payroll tax returns and reports
Discuss the nature of long-term assets (tangible assets, intangible assets, natural resources, etc.)
Describe the methods used to value long-term assets
Account for long-term assets (record acquisition, record depreciation/amortization, record disposal)
Account for long-term liabilities (bonds payable, notes payable, leases, etc.)
Account for provisions (restructurings, warranties, customer refunds, etc.)
Explain record keeping procedures for tax accounting
Calculate taxes owed by clients (individual and business)
Account for taxes
Prepare tax returns for clients (individuals and business)
Identify tax issues for clients
Differentiate among management accounting responsibility centers (cost, profit, investment, revenue)
Discuss the use of cost-volume-profit analysis
Discuss cost accounting systems (job costing, process costing, standard costing, activity-based costing)
Distinguish between variable costing and absorption costing
Describe common management accounting performance measures (balanced scorecard, ROI, customer profitability analysis, etc.)
Discuss the role of standard costing in the preparation and analysis of budgets
Describe the nature of flexible budgets
Explain the role of transfer pricing in managerial accounting
Explain the impact of business operational practices (TQM, lean production, JIT, etc.) on managerial accounting
Discuss the nature of annual reports
Analyze transactions and accounts (purchase, sales, sales returns and allowances, uncollectible accounts, depreciation, debt)
Explain the purpose of internal accounting controls
Assess financial accounting fraud risk
Determine the components of internal accounting control procedures for a business
Maintain internal accounting controls
Explain the nature of audits and assurance engagements
Distinguish between internal and external audits
Describe auditing techniques/procedures
Conduct audit engagements
Maintain job order cost sheets
Calculate the cost of goods sold
Apply cost accounting techniques (job costing, process costing, standard costing, activity-based costing)
Explain types of budgeting systems (top-down, bottom-up, incremental, etc.)
Project future revenues and expenses
Process preliminary budget detail

Information Management (NF).standard: Understands tools, strategies, and systems needed to access, process, maintain, evaluate, and disseminate information to assist business decision-making

indicators.text: Use accounting applications and systems
Describe the nature of Extensible Business Reporting Language (XBRL)
Integrate technology into accounting
Preserve automated accounting records
Select confidence levels
Test data for definitive relationships
Test data for definitive associations
Test data for meaningful differences
Use statistical data inferences to draw preliminary conclusions
Identify types of data analysis modeling techniques
Apply mathematical data analysis modeling techniques
Use data analysis software
Explain the use of descriptive statistics in business decision making
Interpret descriptive statistics for business decision making
Interpret business data correlations
Draw conclusions on the research question/issue

Operations (OP).standard: Understands the processes and systems implemented to monitor, plan, and control the day-to-day activities required for continued business functioning

indicators.text: Discuss the connection between business analysis and business process management
Explain types of requirements (business, system, functional, nonfunctional)
Document business processes
Identify the business process problem/issue
Define data needs and limitations (data fields, constraints, assumptions, variations expectations)
Identify data acquisition strategies
Analyze business processes (measure efficiency, benchmark metrics)
Recommend improvements to business processes

Professional Development (PD).standard: Understands concepts, tools, and strategies used to explore, obtain, and develop in a business career

indicators.text: Identify career opportunities in accounting
Explain the roles and responsibilities of accounting professionals
Discuss professional designations for accountants (CPA, CMA, CIA, CFE, etc.)
Describe the services of professional organizations in accounting
Explain the nature of accounting standards
Discuss the roles and responsibilities of accounting-standards-setting bodies (SEC, FASB, IASB, GASB)
Compare U.S. Generally Accepted Accounting Principles (GAAP) and International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS)
Discuss the levels and types of external financial reporting
Discuss the nature of auditing/attestation standards
